title: RBACv2-aware audit stream sharding: coldspill mitigation and cost signal pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement RBAC v2-aware shard assignment and a lightweight cost-signal pipeline for audit ingestion to reduce coldstore spill events and long-term storage spend while preserving an auditable trail for SSO/SAML and admin actions.

Background: Our audit ingestion stream has shown periodic spikes that cause hot partitions and subsequent coldspill events, inflating read/write amplification and unexpected egress costs. With RBAC v2 we add per-tenant and per-role enrichment that increases event cardinality. We need a coordinated approach that: 1) assigns shards in a way that avoids RBAC/SSO-driven hotspots, 2) tags events for TTL/index tiering decisions, and 3) emits a cost-signal metric that downstream storage controllers can consume.

Scope:
- Extend ingest router to support RBAC v2 metadata-aware shard keys (tenant_id + role_bucket).
- Add an enrichment step that attaches storage_class_hint and retention_bucket fields (enumerated: hot, warm, cold) at ingest time.
- Implement an async cost-signal producer that aggregates ingest token counts, KV cache hit rates, and shard spill events and writes a compact report to the internal metrics topic (for controller consumption).
- Update indexer policy to pick indexing granularity based on retention_bucket and recent cost_signals.
- Ensure SSO/SAML admin events (sensitive) are always routed to immutable hotstore for 30 days before tiering.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in 95th percentile ingest latency > 15ms for median-sized events after RBAC enrichment (baseline measured).
- Coldspill event frequency on test tenants reduced by >= 60% in the first 7 days post-rollout (compared to control).
- Storage controller responds to cost_signal messages and moves >= 80% of warm->cold eligible shards within SLA window.
- Audit trail preserved: every retention change leaves an immutable audit record with SAML/SSO user id and role.

Out-of-scope: Backfilling historical events for new retention buckets; separate long-term analytics indexes (handled by analytics team).

Key trade-offs considered:
- Enriching at ingest vs. post-ingest classification: We choose ingest enrichment to enable immediate routing and TTL decisions at the cost of small CPU/latency overhead; mitigated by sampling and lightweight role_bucket hashing.
- Deterministic sharding vs. probabilistic balancing: deterministic tenant+role avoids cross-tenant leaks and simplifies compliance; we will add a periodic rebalancer to compensate for skew.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary enrich-only on 5% of traffic with opt-out header.
2) Enable shard assignment policy for canary tenants and run cost-signal producer.
3) Monitor ingest latency, coldspill rate, and retention audit records for 72 hours.
4) Gradual ramp to 100% with automated rollback if coldspill rate regresses above threshold.

Metrics & dashboards:
- grafana: /d/ops/audit-ingest-shards (ingest_latency_p95, coldspill_count, storage_moved_bytes)
- bigquery: audit_cost_signals.daily

Compliance notes: SSO/SAML admin events are marked sensitive and require the RBAC v2 policy to prevent cross-tenant exposure. Keys for these markers are immutable once written.
